dialogue.content: （こんにちは、準備が出来ましたらお声掛けください。よろしくお願いいたします）
dialogue.English: (Hello, please let me know when you're ready. I look forward to our session.)

dialogue.content: よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: I look forward to it as well.

dialogue.content: （少し早いですが、よろしければスタートさせていただきます。いかがですか？）
dialogue.English: (It's a little early, but if it's alright with you, we can begin. How does that sound?)

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: こんにちは、相談員です。今日はどのようなご相談をなさりたいですか？
dialogue.English: Hello, I'm your counselor. What would you like to discuss today?

dialogue.content: 職場の人間関係です。
dialogue.English: It's about workplace relationships.

dialogue.content: そうですか、承知しました。お話を伺うにあたって、できる範囲で年齢、性別、お名前を教えてください。
dialogue.English: I see, I understand. To start, could you please tell me your age, gender, and the name you’d like me to use, to the extent you're comfortable?

dialogue.content: 40代女性です。名前はMでお願いします。
dialogue.English: I'm a woman in my 40s. Please call me M.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます、Ｍさん。人間関係というと、同僚の方とのことなどでしょうか？出来事などあれば聞かせていただけますか？
dialogue.English: Thank you, M. When you say relationships, are you referring to colleagues? If there have been any specific incidents, could you tell me about them?

dialogue.content: 同僚なのですが、業務上必要なことも、私には伝えてくれず、とにかく無視です。
dialogue.English: It's a coworker. They don't communicate things that are necessary for work to me; they just completely ignore me.

dialogue.content: それはお気持ち的にもお仕事的にも大変なことですね、きっかけのような事はおもいあたりますか？
dialogue.English: That must be very difficult for you, both emotionally and for your work. Can you think of anything that might have triggered this?

dialogue.content: それが…思い当たらなくて。4月から徐々に進行してきた感じです（4月に移動で来られてからです。）
dialogue.English: That's the thing... I can't think of anything. It feels like it's been gradually getting worse since April (since they transferred to our department in April).

dialogue.content: 新しく仲間になられた方なんですね。きっかけが分からないと、Ｍさんも対処に困りますよね・・・
dialogue.English: So they are a new member of the team. Not knowing what caused it must make it very difficult for you to know how to handle it...

dialogue.content: はい。
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 周りの方はそのことをどう見ておられますか？上司の方や先輩のような方たちにご相談はされてますか？
dialogue.English: How do others around you see this situation? Have you talked to your boss or any senior colleagues about it?

dialogue.content: 上司や、課の責任者には積極的に話すので理解してもらえなくて。
dialogue.English: They talk proactively to the boss and the department head, so they don't understand my side of the story.

dialogue.content: 私と、もう一人にだけ無視なのです。
dialogue.English: It's just me and one other person they ignore.

dialogue.content: いってもいいですか？
dialogue.English: Can I just say it?

dialogue.content: なるほど、相手の方は上司にははきはきされるタイプにみえているんですね、Ｍさんに対する冷たい仕打ちが見えていないように思います。
dialogue.English: I see. So this person appears to be articulate and assertive with superiors. It seems they don't see the cold treatment towards you.

dialogue.content: はい、どうぞ
dialogue.English: Yes, please go ahead.

dialogue.content: だいきらい！です
dialogue.English: I really hate them!

dialogue.content: そうですよね、意地悪な感じが私にも伝わります！
dialogue.English: I can understand that. The meanness comes across to me even from what you've said!

dialogue.content: 自分が悪いのかなと感じてて、気持ちを押し込めようとしたのですが・・・だいきらい！
dialogue.English: I was starting to feel like maybe I was the one at fault, and I tried to suppress my feelings... but I really hate them!

dialogue.content: なんかすっきりします
dialogue.English: Somehow, I feel refreshed.

dialogue.content: 良かったです！時には気持ちを開放することは大切です！相手の方(女性？）のどんなところをＭさんが大嫌いと感じるところでしょう？
dialogue.English: I'm glad! It's important to release your feelings sometimes! What is it about this person (are they a woman?) that makes you hate them so much, M?

dialogue.content: 無視以外にもなにかありますか？
dialogue.English: Besides ignoring you, is there anything else?

dialogue.content: 姑息なやり方だと思うのです。無視なんて
dialogue.English: I think it's such a cowardly way to act. Just ignoring someone.

dialogue.content: ほかにはないですね。休憩中も私ともう一人と一緒になったとたんだんまりされます
dialogue.English: There's nothing else, really. During breaks, if they end up with me and the other person, they just go completely silent.

dialogue.content: そうですよね、意地悪だしＭさんともう一人の方の気持ちをないがしろにしていますね。
dialogue.English: I agree, that's malicious and completely disregards your feelings and the other person's.

dialogue.content: なるほど、そういう日常はイライラしたりムカムカして休まらないことだと思います。
dialogue.English: I see. Living with that every day must be frustrating and upsetting; I imagine you can't get any peace.

dialogue.content: それでも仕事ができれば、まだ認めるところもあるのですが、仕事も緻密さに欠けてて…フォローが大変です。
dialogue.English: If they were at least good at their job, there would be something to respect, but their work lacks precision... it's a lot of effort to cover for them.

dialogue.content: でも理想は高いのです。
dialogue.English: But they have high ideals.

dialogue.content: その方のフォローまでされるんですか！？
dialogue.English: You even have to cover for that person's work!?

dialogue.content: チームですから、仕方ないです。同じ平なので。
dialogue.English: We're a team, so I have to. We're at the same level.

dialogue.content: なるほど、共同作業と言うか、フォローしあって進めるお仕事なんですね、なおの事心がざわざわしてしまいそうですね。
dialogue.English: I see, so it's a job where you have to collaborate and support each other to move forward. That must make things even more unsettling for you.

dialogue.content: 報告などがないので、私のミスになることもあります。
dialogue.English: Since they don't give me reports, sometimes it ends up looking like my mistake.

dialogue.content: それは、その方が嘘をついてＭさんのせいにすると言う事ですか？
dialogue.English: Do you mean that person lies and blames you, M?

dialogue.content: 連絡が無いからＭさんの仕事がきちんと進まなかったと言う事でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Or is it that because there was no communication, you couldn't proceed with your work properly?

dialogue.content: 聞いていないので、要求も知らずに顧客に対応することになったり。です。
dialogue.English: Since I haven't been told, I sometimes end up dealing with clients without knowing their requests.

dialogue.content: 上司には　”あれ～　言いましたよ”なんて伝えているので、余計に私のミスだと思われて
dialogue.English: They tell our boss things like, "Oh? I did tell her," so it makes it look even more like my mistake.

dialogue.content: それは他の方からすると「聞いてないの？」と言う感じで、Ｍさんは悪くないのに嫌な印象を与えてしまう事になりますね、嫌な思いをされましたね
dialogue.English: So to other people, it looks like you "didn't listen," which gives a bad impression even though you did nothing wrong. That must have felt terrible.

dialogue.content: 職場に4月から来た人ということで、転勤や配置換えなどで距離をとれる可能性は少ないのかと思いますが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: Since this person just arrived at your workplace in April, I imagine the chances of you being able to get some distance through a transfer or reassignment are low. Is that correct?

dialogue.content: このままだと、ずっと一緒か、私が移動になるかです。私は、あまり上司と業務以外の話はしないので余計にそうなるのかもしれません。
dialogue.English: If things stay as they are, we'll either be together indefinitely, or I'll be the one who gets transferred. I don't really talk to my boss about things outside of work, so that might make it more likely.

dialogue.content: そうなんですね、職場の所属と言うのは自分の意志だけで変えられないのが辛いところですよね。
dialogue.English: I see. The difficult part about workplace assignments is that you can't change them just by your own will.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: お話を伺っていて、これからＭさんがどう職場生活を送れたらよいのかをご一緒に考えたいと思っています。
dialogue.English: As I've been listening to you, I'd like to work with you to figure out how you can best navigate your life at work from now on.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 気持ちが軽く、お仕事に集中できる方法を探してみましょう！
dialogue.English: Let's look for a way for you to feel lighter and be able to concentrate on your work!

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Okay.

dialogue.content: 先ずは、一般的にどんな方でもどうしても「馬の合わない人」というのは存在すると思うのです。
dialogue.English: First of all, I think it's generally true that for anyone, there are always people you just don't get along with.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: 特にＭさんが積極的に嫌ったり、嫌なことをしたわけではないので、相手が理由なく嫌な感情になってしまう事も残念ながらあることなのだと思います
dialogue.English: And since it's not like you actively disliked them or did anything unpleasant to them, I think it's unfortunately possible for someone to develop negative feelings for no clear reason.

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: Yes.

dialogue.content: ないのに　　でした
dialogue.English: I meant, "even though you didn't."

dialogue.content: はい
dialogue.English: I see.

dialogue.content: 先ずはお仕事の側面だけでも上司の方に対処していただけたらと思うのですが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: To begin with, I was thinking it would be good if your boss could at least address the work-related aspects of this. What do you think?

dialogue.content: 上司は事なかれ主義で、どうすれば、チームで、心地よく仕事できるか自分たちで話し合って、だの。チームワークのために何ができるかだの。
dialogue.English: My boss is the type to avoid conflict, and just says things like, "You all should discuss among yourselves how to work comfortably as a team," or "Think about what you can do for teamwork."

dialogue.content: そういう感じのひとなんですね、頼りがいを感じられないとお考えですよね、わかる気がします。
dialogue.English: So that's the kind of person they are. You must feel you can't rely on them. I can understand that.

dialogue.content: 班長も、あなたたちの問題でしょ？って感じです。とにかく、自分よりも上か、自分よりもぐんと年下には穏やかに話すので。
dialogue.English: The team leader is also like, "That's your problem, isn't it?" The thing is, they speak gently to people above them or those who are much younger.

dialogue.content: なので、私ともう一人の性格の問題だと思われていて。
dialogue.English: So, it's seen as a personality problem between me and the other person.

dialogue.content: なるほど、相手の方も空気を読めるようなところがあるんですね、うまく立ち回ると言うか・・・
dialogue.English: I see, so the other person is good at reading the room, so to speak... they know how to handle situations to their advantage.

dialogue.content: 本社に相談します！というと少し慌てるものの、解決策はなしです。
dialogue.English: When I say, "I'm going to consult with the head office!" they get a little flustered, but there's no resolution.

dialogue.content: そうなんです！パワハラ相談窓口などは会社にないのでしょうか？
dialogue.English: Exactly! Doesn't your company have a consultation service for power harassment?

dialogue.content: 理解者がいないので。ほかのチームはかかわりたくないので、大変だね～で終わります。
dialogue.English: There's no one who understands. Other teams don't want to get involved, so it just ends with them saying, "Oh, that sounds tough."

dialogue.content: パワハラは同僚同志にもあります。今、探してみたのですが、判断基準の一つに「著しい苦痛を与え、職場環境を乱しているか」という記述もありました。Ｍさんともう一人の方の状態はこれに近くはありませんか？
dialogue.English: Power harassment can happen between colleagues as well. I just looked it up, and one of the criteria is whether it "causes significant distress and disrupts the work environment." Don't you think the situation you and the other person are in is close to this?

dialogue.content: そうですが、人手が足りないので、よくて、私が移動ですかね。
dialogue.English: It is, but we're short-staffed, so at best, I'd be the one to get transferred, I suppose.

dialogue.content: https://hataractive.jp/useful/456/このサイトにありました。会社のコンプライアンスやハラスメント相談などで対処が良いと思ったのですが・・・難しい体制なのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: I found it on this website: https://hataractive.jp/useful/456/. I thought handling it through the company's compliance or harassment consultation services would be a good approach, but... is the system difficult to use?

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: Ｍさんとしては、この職場以外のところに相談するなどの方法で相手の方の横暴を止めたいとお考えでえすか？
dialogue.English: M, are you thinking you want to stop this person's outrageous behavior by consulting with someone outside of your immediate workplace?

dialogue.content: それとも、どちらかが転勤などで距離をとれるまで、ご自分の心をコントロールして過ごす方が現実的ですか？
dialogue.English: Or is it more realistic to control your own emotions and get by until one of you can get some distance through a transfer?

dialogue.content: 何が何でもとは思いません。これ以上かかわりたくないというのが本音です。なんか情けなくなるので。
dialogue.English: I'm not thinking I have to do something at all costs. My true feeling is that I just don't want to have anything more to do with them. It just makes me feel pathetic.

dialogue.content: はい。そうですね。自分の気持ちをコントロールするほうが現実的です。ミスになることは避けたいですが。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's right. Controlling my own feelings is more realistic. But I want to avoid situations that result in them becoming my mistake.

dialogue.content: そうですね、どんなに大変な相手でも目の前にいる以上、エネルギーをつかいますよね。
dialogue.English: That's true. No matter how difficult the person is, as long as they're right in front of you, it takes a lot of energy.

dialogue.content: 本当に。だいきらいです。
dialogue.English: It really does. I hate them.

dialogue.content: そうですね、そんな気持ちがしても当然の状況におられると思います。そして、私は思うのですが、同僚といえども好きにらなければいけない決まりはないのです！
dialogue.English: Yes, I think you're in a situation where it's completely natural to feel that way. And I believe that even if someone is your colleague, there's no rule that says you have to like them!

dialogue.content: すきにはなれない。ただ、平穏に一日を終えたい。
dialogue.English: I can't bring myself to like them. I just want to end the day peacefully.

dialogue.content: Ｍさんの「嫌い！」という気持ちと、お仕事を最低限しっかり進めると言う事を分けて行動できれば問題が小さくなるように思いますが、いかがですか？
dialogue.English: If you could separate your feeling of "I hate them!" from the act of carrying out your minimum work duties, it seems like the problem might get smaller. What do you think?

dialogue.content: そうなのですか？報告などはどうすればいいですか？文字にしてもらうなどの方法でしょうか？
dialogue.English: Is that so? What should I do about reports and things? Should I try a method like having them put it in writing?

dialogue.content: 嫌いはそのままで、無理に変えなくて良いと思うのです。ただ、「仕事上の連絡をしない」というような意地悪を止めることですよね
dialogue.English: I think you can leave the dislike as it is; you don't need to force yourself to change it. The key is to stop the malicious behavior, like their "not communicating for work purposes," right?

dialogue.content: はい。それだけでいいです。
dialogue.English: Yes. That's all I want.

dialogue.content: お仕事の状態が分からないのですが、Ｍさんがおっしゃった通り「伝言メモ」などの引継ぎツールのようなものをチーム全体で導入してもらったらいかがでしょうか？
dialogue.English: I'm not familiar with your work setup, but as you suggested, how about having the whole team adopt a handover tool, like a 'message memo' system?

dialogue.content: ＰＣにもそういった機能はあるのですが、交換日記や雑記帳のように一冊ノートを置いておくのも良いかもしれません
dialogue.English: There are functions like that on PCs, but it might also be a good idea to keep a single notebook, like a shared journal or logbook.

dialogue.content: そうですね。忙しくしてるときにいなくなってしまうことも多々あるのですが、班長に呼びに行ってもらってもいいですかね？
dialogue.English: That's a good idea. They often disappear when we're busy. Do you think it would be okay to ask the team leader to go get them?

dialogue.content: 相手の方が意地悪を続けると、極端に伝言が少ないことが「見える化」できるのでばれてしまうと思うのです。
dialogue.English: If the other person continues to be malicious, the extreme lack of messages will become 'visible,' so I think they will be found out.

dialogue.content: それはもちろん、良いことだと思います！
dialogue.English: Yes, of course, I think that's a great idea!

dialogue.content: わかりました。やってみます。ありがとうございました。なにより、だいきらい！といえて、すっきりしました。
dialogue.English: I understand. I'll try it. Thank you. Most of all, I feel so much better being able to say, "I hate them!"

dialogue.content: 良かったです！
dialogue.English: I'm so glad!

dialogue.content: https://tech-camp.in/note/careerchange/40100/
dialogue.English: https://tech-camp.in/note/careerchange/40100/

dialogue.content: 因みにこのサイトは「職場の嫌な人との付き合い方」と言うサイトです
dialogue.English: By the way, this site is called "How to Deal with Difficult People at Work."

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。参考にしてみます。
dialogue.English: Thank you. I'll take a look at it.

dialogue.content: こんなページがアップされていると言う事はＭさんのような悩みがある方が世の中にいっぱいいると言う事だと思います。辛い日もあると思いますが、「大丈夫！みんなも辛い時がある！」とご自身を抱きしめてあげて下さい
dialogue.English: The fact that pages like this are online means there are many people in the world with the same worries as you. I'm sure you'll have tough days, but please give yourself a hug and tell yourself, "It's okay! Everyone has hard times!"

dialogue.content: それではそろそろ時間となりますが、話足りないことなどありませんか？
dialogue.English: Well, our time is almost up. Is there anything else you feel you haven't had a chance to say?

dialogue.content: ありません。なんかすっきりしました。
dialogue.English: No, there isn't. I feel somewhat relieved.

dialogue.content: 良かったです！私にもこの一時間で元気に職場で活躍されるＭさんが見えてきた気がします！また、困ったことがあればお越しください。お話聞かせていただきます！
dialogue.English: I'm glad! In this past hour, I feel like I've been able to see a vision of you thriving energetically at your workplace! Please come back again if you run into any trouble. I'll be here to listen!

dialogue.content: 心強いです。
dialogue.English: That's very reassuring.

dialogue.content: おいでくださってありがとうございました！
dialogue.English: Thank you very much for coming today!

dialogue.content: では、この辺で失礼いたします。（ロープレありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: Well then, I'll take my leave. (Thank you for the role-play.)

dialogue.content: 大変勉強になりました。ありがとうございました。
dialogue.English: This was very insightful. Thank you very much.

dialogue.content: 失礼します
dialogue.English: Goodbye.

dialogue.content: （ありがとうございました）
dialogue.English: (Thank you.)
